# kcore_cluster_version (Resource)

The kcore release every node runs (`kctl update version set`). Changing `version` starts a rollout: by default a canary node updates and soaks while the controller compares it with the other nodes, then the rest update one at a time. Another version is refused while a rollout runs. Destroy only forgets the resource; nodes keep their version.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kcore_cluster_version" "this" {
  version             = "v0.7.0"
  drain_vms           = true
  canary_soak_seconds = 14400
  canary_node         = "node-b"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `version` (String) Release tag, `v0.7.0` or `0.7.0`.

### Optional

- `canary_node` (String) The canary. Empty picks a node labelled `kcore.io/update-canary`, else the first node in rollout order. A node that runs a controller is refused unless every node does.
- `canary_soak_seconds` (Number) How long the canary soaks. 0 means 24 hours when the release moves to another NixOS release and one hour otherwise. At most 7 days.
- `drain_vms` (Boolean) Migrate guests off a node before it reboots into a new kernel.
- `flake_ref` (String) Repository the tag is resolved in. Empty means `github:kcorehypervisor/kcore`; an air-gapped site names its mirror.
- `no_canary` (Boolean) Update every node one at a time with no canary and no soak.

### Read-Only

- `canary_node_id` (String) The canary the last change picked. Empty without a canary or when nothing changed.
- `flake_rev` (String) Commit the tag resolved to.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `phase` (String) Phase of that rollout.
- `update_name` (String) ClusterUpdate of the latest rollout.
